q: The noise level rises from $85\,\text{dB}$ to $95\,\text{dB}$. How many times greater is the intensity, and in how long does the same dose build up as in $8\,\text{h}$ at a level of $85\,\text{dB}$?
a: A rise of $10\,\text{dB}$ corresponds to ten times the intensity (chapter *Intensity and the decibel scale*). The same energy builds up in a tenth of the time: $480\,\text{min} : 10 = 48\,\text{min}$. The rule of thumb $t_\text{perm} = t_0 / 2^{\,n}$ gives the same: $n = 10/3$ and $t_\text{perm} \approx 48\,\text{min}$.

q: After a concert the ears ring, but by morning the ringing has gone. Does that mean that hearing was not damaged?
a: Not necessarily. Ringing and temporary dulling of hearing show that the hair cells of the inner ear were strained. Hearing may recover almost fully, but repeated strain leads to permanent hearing loss and may cause permanent tinnitus, because hair cells do not regenerate.
